name: Albania
hint: a small Balkan country on the Adriatic and Ionian coasts, north-west of Greece
facts: Albania's flag shows a black double-headed eagle on red.
Albanians call their country Shqipëria.

name: Andorra
hint: a tiny mountain country in the Pyrenees, between France and Spain
facts: Andorra's official language is Catalan.
Andorra la Vella is the highest capital city in Europe.
hint2: People here speak Catalan, high in the mountains.

name: Austria
hint: an Alpine country whose capital sits on the River Danube
facts: Mozart was born in Salzburg, Austria.
The Alps cover much of Austria.

name: Belarus
hint: a landlocked country between Poland and Russia
facts: Belarus has no coastline.
European bison live in the ancient Białowieża Forest on the Belarus-Poland border.

name: Belgium
hint: a small country between France and the Netherlands, famous for waffles and chocolate
facts: Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French, and German.
Many of the European Union's main offices are in Brussels.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
hint: a Balkan country with only a tiny strip of coast on the Adriatic
facts: Mostar is famous for its arched Old Bridge over the Neretva River.
Sarajevo hosted the Winter Olympics in 1984.

name: Bulgaria
hint: a Balkan country on the Black Sea, just south of Romania
facts: Bulgaria's Rose Valley is famous for rose oil used in perfume.
Bulgaria writes its language in the Cyrillic alphabet.

name: Croatia
hint: a crescent-shaped country on the Adriatic with more than a thousand islands
facts: The necktie traces back to scarves worn by Croatian soldiers.
Dubrovnik is famous for its old stone city walls.

name: Czechia
hint: a landlocked central European country that was once joined with Slovakia
facts: Prague's astronomical clock dates from 1410.
Czechia and Slovakia split peacefully in 1993.

name: Denmark
hint: a Scandinavian country made of a peninsula north of Germany and many islands
facts: LEGO bricks come from Denmark.
Hans Christian Andersen, who wrote The Little Mermaid, was Danish.

name: Estonia
hint: the northernmost of the three Baltic countries
facts: Around half of Estonia is covered in forest.
People in Estonia can vote in national elections online.

name: Finland
hint: a Nordic country of tens of thousands of lakes, east of Sweden
facts: Finland has more than 100,000 lakes.
Saunas are a big part of life in Finland.

name: France
hint: the country just north of Spain, on the far side of the Pyrenees mountains
facts: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was built for a world's fair in 1889.
Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps, stands on the France-Italy border.

name: Germany
hint: the central European country with the most people in the European Union
facts: The Berlin Wall came down in 1989.
Germany has more people than any other country in the European Union.

name: Greece
hint: the southern end of the Balkan Peninsula, among thousands of islands
facts: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.
Greece has thousands of islands in the Aegean and Ionian Seas.

name: Hungary
hint: a landlocked country where the Danube runs through the middle of its capital
facts: Budapest was formed by joining the cities of Buda and Pest.
The Rubik's Cube was invented in Hungary.

name: Iceland
hint: an island of volcanoes and geysers in the North Atlantic
facts: Reykjavik is the northernmost capital of any country in the world.
The English word geyser comes from Geysir, a hot spring in Iceland.

name: Ireland
hint: an island country west of Great Britain, known for its green fields
facts: The harp is the national symbol of Ireland.
Halloween traces back to the old Irish festival of Samhain.

name: Italy
hint: the boot-shaped country reaching into the Mediterranean Sea
facts: Italy completely surrounds both San Marino and Vatican City.
Pizza as we know it comes from Naples, Italy.

name: Latvia
hint: the middle one of the three Baltic countries
facts: Riga's old town is famous for its Art Nouveau buildings.
Amber washes up on Latvia's Baltic beaches.

name: Liechtenstein
hint: a tiny Alpine country squeezed between Switzerland and Austria
facts: Liechtenstein is one of only two countries surrounded entirely by landlocked countries.
Vaduz Castle, above the capital, is home to the prince.

name: Lithuania
hint: the southernmost of the three Baltic countries
facts: In 1990 Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence.
Basketball is the favorite sport in Lithuania.

name: Luxembourg
hint: a tiny grand duchy bordered by Belgium, France, and Germany
facts: Luxembourg is the only grand duchy left in the world.
Public transport in Luxembourg is free.
hint2: This tiny country is the only grand duchy left in the world.

name: Malta
hint: a tiny island country in the Mediterranean, south of Sicily
facts: Maltese is the only Semitic language that is official in the European Union.
Valletta is one of the smallest capital cities in Europe.

name: Moldova
hint: a landlocked country between Romania and Ukraine
facts: Moldova's Mileștii Mici has the largest wine cellars in the world.
Most people in Moldova speak Romanian.

name: Monaco
hint: a tiny country on the French Riviera
facts: Monaco is the second smallest country in the world.
Cars race through the streets of Monaco in a famous Grand Prix.
hint2: Monte Carlo is one of the districts of this tiny country.

name: Montenegro
hint: a small mountainous country on the Adriatic, south of Bosnia
facts: The Bay of Kotor in Montenegro looks like a fjord.
The Tara River Canyon in Montenegro is the deepest in Europe.

name: Netherlands
hint: a flat country of canals and windmills, with much of its land below sea level
facts: About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level.
The Netherlands is famous for its tulip fields.

name: North Macedonia
hint: a landlocked Balkan country just north of Greece
facts: Mother Teresa was born in Skopje.
Lake Ohrid is one of the oldest lakes in Europe.

name: Norway
hint: a long, narrow Scandinavian country with deep fjords on the Atlantic
facts: Norway's fjords were carved by glaciers.
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo.

name: Poland
hint: a large country on the Baltic, between Germany and Belarus
facts: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw.
Nicolaus Copernicus, who showed that Earth orbits the Sun, was born in Poland.

name: Portugal
hint: the country directly west of Spain, facing the Atlantic Ocean
facts: Portugal produces more cork than any other country.
Explorer Vasco da Gama sailed from Portugal to India.

name: Romania
hint: a country on the Black Sea, curved around the Carpathian Mountains
facts: Bran Castle in Romania is linked to the legend of Dracula.
The River Danube reaches the sea in Romania's Danube Delta.

name: Russia
hint: the largest country in the world, stretching across Europe and Asia
facts: Russia is the largest country in the world.
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world.

name: San Marino
hint: a tiny country on the slopes of Mount Titano
facts: San Marino claims to be the oldest republic in the world.
San Marino is completely surrounded by Italy.
hint2: This tiny country claims to be the oldest republic in the world.

name: Serbia
hint: a landlocked Balkan country where the River Sava meets the Danube
facts: Belgrade stands where the River Sava joins the Danube.
Tennis star Novak Djokovic was born in Belgrade.

name: Slovakia
hint: a landlocked country east of Czechia, home of the High Tatra mountains
facts: Bratislava sits right beside the borders of Austria and Hungary.
The High Tatras are the tallest part of the Carpathian Mountains.

name: Slovenia
hint: a small country between Italy and Croatia, with a very short Adriatic coast
facts: Lake Bled in Slovenia has a tiny church on its island.
Postojna Cave in Slovenia is home to pale cave salamanders called olms.

name: Spain
hint: the larger of the two countries on the Iberian Peninsula
facts: The Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882.
Spain shares the Iberian Peninsula with Portugal.

name: Sweden
hint: the largest Scandinavian country, between Norway and the Baltic Sea
facts: Most Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.
IKEA was founded in Sweden.

name: Switzerland
hint: an Alpine country with four national languages
facts: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh.
The Swiss flag is square.

name: Ukraine
hint: the largest country entirely inside Europe, on the Black Sea
facts: Ukraine is the largest country entirely inside Europe.
Ukraine's flag is often described as blue sky over yellow wheat.

name: United Kingdom
hint: a country mostly on the island of Great Britain, across the English Channel from France
facts: The United Kingdom is made up of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
Big Ben is the great bell in the clock tower at London's Palace of Westminster.

name: Vatican City
hint: the smallest country in the world, inside the city of Rome
facts: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.
The Swiss Guard has protected the Pope for more than 500 years.
hint2: This tiny country is home to the Pope and St. Peter's Basilica.
